premise: A fictional, self-deprecating stickman prop-firm trader keeps blowing challenges to revenge trades. Across 3 shorts he discovers the real lesson is a habit (log with stops, tag mistakes honestly, review weekly), with TradeNotes as the tool that organizes it. No outcome promises; comedic dramatization.

videos.working_title: One Revenge Trade Ended My Challenge
videos.hook_text_overlay: Blew my prop challenge in ONE trade
videos.saveable_takeaway: Your stop defines 1R. If a loss is bigger than -1R, the problem isn't the market.
videos.feature_mentioned: Manual trade logging (entry/stop/exit) with automatic R-multiple

beats.vo: I blew my prop challenge with one trade. Again.
beats.scene: Stickman at desk, chart behind him; one giant red candle drops and flattens him like a cartoon anvil. Text overlay: 'BLEW MY CHALLENGE IN ONE TRADE'. Fast punch-in.

beats.vo: Green all morning. Then one red trade, and I wanted that money back. Immediately.
beats.scene: Stickman sipping coffee, smug, green P&L ticker. Small red tick appears; his eye twitches, coffee cup cracks. Whip-zoom to his face.

beats.vo: Doubled size. Moved my stop. [sighs] Daily loss limit: breached.
beats.scene: Stickman slams a 'SIZE x2' button, drags his stop line further away with both arms; a red 'DAILY LIMIT BREACHED' stamp hits the screen. Camera shake.

beats.vo: So, like a genius, I paid for a reset and did the exact same thing.
beats.scene: Stickman feeds coins into a 'RESET' vending machine, gets a fresh account, immediately repeats the same slam/drag motions in sped-up replay. Small caption: 'fictional dramatization'.

beats.vo: Then I started logging every trade in TradeNotes: entry, stop, exit. It works out the R-multiple.
beats.scene: Stickman at a clean screen typing entry/stop/exit fields into a TradeNotes-style trade form; an 'R' badge pops up next to the row.

beats.vo: My stop said minus one R. My revenge trade? Minus four R.
beats.scene: Split screen: neat '-1R' label vs a huge wobbling '-4R' that squishes the stickman. Slow push-in on '-4R'.

beats.vo: But logging wasn't the real needle mover. It was something way dumber. Part two.
beats.scene: Stickman holds a lightbulb that flickers off; he looks at camera, shrugs; '?' and 'PART 2' card slides in.

videos.working_title: I Tagged My Bad Trades. I Was the Problem.
videos.hook_text_overlay: Tagged my bad trades. Found the problem: me

beats.vo: Tagged my bad trades. The problem? Me.
beats.scene: Stickman pins a red tag labelled 'PROBLEM' on a chart, it boomerangs back and sticks to his forehead. Overlay: 'TAGGED MY BAD TRADES'.

beats.vo: Logging trades was step one. The real needle mover was tagging them.
beats.scene: Stickman holds a logbook, then swaps it for a label gun like it's a weapon upgrade. Quick tilt-up.

beats.vo: Every bad trade got an honest tag. Revenge trade. Moved stop. FOMO.
beats.scene: Label gun fires tags onto trade rows: 'REVENGE', 'MOVED STOP', 'FOMO', each with a tiny cartoon of stickman's crime.

beats.vo: Then I filtered my journal by mistake tag in TradeNotes. [laughs] Oh no.
beats.scene: TradeNotes-style journal list; stickman clicks a 'Revenge trade' filter; list collapses to a wall of red rows. His jaw hits the floor.

beats.vo: My worst losses weren't bad luck. They were trades I knew were bad while clicking.
beats.scene: Flashback: stickman with angry eyebrows mashing BUY while a tiny angel stickman on his shoulder holds a 'NO' sign.

beats.vo: Not the market. Not the firm. Me. Mad. Clicking.
beats.scene: Three spotlights: market (empty), firm building (empty), stickman (caught mid-click, steam from ears).

beats.vo: So how do you stop the idiot before he clicks? Part three.
beats.scene: Stickman's hand hovers over BUY in slow motion; freeze frame; 'PART 3' card slams in.

videos.working_title: The 3-Step Habit That Ended My One-More-Trade Spiral
videos.hook_text_overlay: The 3-step habit that ended my 'one more trade'
videos.saveable_takeaway: 1) Log every trade with its stop. 2) Tag every mistake honestly. 3) Friday: filter by tag, check red days, write one rule.
videos.feature_mentioned: Calendar month view with daily P&L colour; mistake-tag filter; trade logging

beats.vo: Three steps that ended my one-more-trade spiral.
beats.scene: Stickman chained to a slot machine labelled 'ONE MORE TRADE'; he snips the chain with giant scissors. Overlay: '3-STEP HABIT'. Fast zoom.

beats.vo: One: log every trade with its stop. No stop, no trade.
beats.scene: Checklist card '1' flips in; stickman bouncer blocks a trade with no stop line from entering a club.

beats.vo: Two: tag every mistake. Revenge. FOMO. Moved stop.
beats.scene: Card '2'; stickman slaps tags onto his own trades, one tag sticks to his butt.

beats.vo: Three: every Friday, filter by tag and check the calendar view for red days.
beats.scene: Card '3'; TradeNotes-style calendar month view with red and green day tiles; stickman circles the red cluster with a marker.

beats.vo: Then write one rule. Mine: one revenge tag, I'm done for the day.
beats.scene: Stickman writes a sticky note 'REVENGE TAG = DONE', slaps it on monitor, then shuts laptop and walks away whistling.

beats.vo: Nobody can promise you'll pass. It just makes your pattern hard to ignore.
beats.scene: Stickman holds a mirror; reflection shows the angry clicking version of himself, who waves awkwardly.

beats.vo: I built TradeNotes, so I'm biased. Link's in bio. Save this for Friday.
beats.scene: Stickman wears a tiny 'I MADE THIS' badge, shrugs; 'Link in bio' arrow; bookmark icon bounces. Small on-screen disclaimer: 'Not financial advice. Results vary.'

beats.vo: Because Friday-you forgets. Back to step one.
beats.scene: Calendar flips to Friday; stickman scratches head, confused; camera whip-pans back to the slot machine from the hook.
